definition.value: The volumes of the lateral ventricles in the alcoholics are equal to or larger than these volumes in the controls.

spans.text: Based on the observations in , one example of the hypotheses tested in the inter-subject case was: H 0 = “The volumes of the lateral ventricles in the alcoholics are equal to or larger than these volumes in the controls.” Note that as reasoned above, this hypothesis purposely conflicts with established models of alcoholism-related brain changes.
We analyzed images from a sample of seven chronic alcoholic women and 16 control women.
We analyzed images from a sample of seven chronic alcoholic women and 16 control women.

By contrast, one of the hypotheses tested in the intra-subject case was: H 0 = “The volumes of the lateral ventricles increased slower in the alcoholics than in controls.” Because the hypotheses being tested were asymmetric with respect to the direction of the differences between the groups, one-sided tests were used.

value: The cross-sectional inter-subject analysis showed smaller ventricular volumes in alcoholic women than in controls (−33% relative volume for all alcoholics), opposite to the longitudinal findings and to established alcoholism-related effects. It detected group differences in white matter and corpus callosum reduction, but cannot distinguish disease-related changes from natural inter-individual variability or other influences.

value: The longitudinal intra-subject analysis indicated faster ventricular volume increases in alcoholics (+11% per year) than in controls (+2% per year), with the strongest effect in relapsed alcoholics. It also showed cerebrospinal-fluid expansion and white-matter volume loss, and was concluded to be preferable for detecting dynamic disease-related changes because each subject serves as her own control.
